assumptions: The plane elastic constants reuse the existing unmeasured Wood Handbook Douglas-fir material scenario, with both radial and tangential normal bindings. They do not identify growth-ring orientation or actual stock properties.
Strengths retain the frozen C16 intact-section engineering hypothesis and divisors; this is not an NDS allowable assignment or new EC5 load combination.
GcI=0.1 N/mm and equal mode-II energy reuse the earlier explicit all-mode energy hypothesis. GcI=0.05 is an adverse lower-energy sensitivity. No current material measurement is claimed.
The 3.5 mode-II/ mode-I energy ratio follows the published spruce-model convention as a separate sensitivity. It is not a Douglas-fir lower-bound or measured ratio.

The formula is screened only for nonnegative mode magnitudes and grain-parallel, bore-tangent paths in the current sloping finished cleats. A length that fits is not an elastic stress calculation or a resistance proof.

The section action multiplier does not enter this material/process-length domain test. All six source fields are authenticated to ensure unchanged geometry; these are geometry/material scenarios, not 768 new structural load cases.

primary_method.role: Mean-stress method and planar domain; no calibrated spruce resistance is transferred.
